# PrototypeFramework — agent documentation pack

**This directory is the source of truth for everything an AI agent needs to know about the
framework.** It ships inside the UPM package (a `~` folder: on disk, out of the AssetDatabase —
the same mechanism `CodegenManifests~` and `Samples~` already use), so it travels with the pinned
package version and can never disagree with the code a SKU actually resolved.

A SKU does not read this directory directly. `Framework/Agent Docs/Sync` (or
`pf-build.sh agentdocs`) materializes it into the SKU repo, where an agent's context loader
actually looks. See [`sync-contract.md`](./sync-contract.md) for what lands where.

---

## What is here

| File | What it answers | Read when |
|---|---|---|
| [`AGENTS.framework.md`](./AGENTS.framework.md) | The rules. 17 verbatim laws, the human/machine zone, the two View tests, the three-tier init law, the co-dev triage gate. | **Always.** This is the block synced into the SKU's `AGENTS.md`. |
| [`architecture-map.md`](./architecture-map.md) | The shape. Assembly graph, scope tree, boot capabilities, render layers, where each kind of code lives. | Before writing any code that crosses a boundary. |
| [`framework-api.index.json`](./framework-api.index.json) | The lookup. Every public framework type → its assembly → its file path inside the package. **Generated** — regenerated and drift-gated, so it cannot lie. | Instead of grepping. "Where is `IDialogService`?" is one lookup, not a search. |
| [`recipes/`](./recipes/) | The procedures. One file per task shape: manifest to edit → command to run → files you own → gate that must go green. | When doing that exact task. |
| [`skills/`](./skills/) | The on-demand loaders. Each is a `SKILL.md` whose description line stays in context; the body loads only when the task matches. | Never read directly — the sync installs these. |
| [`sync-contract.md`](./sync-contract.md) | Where each file lands in a SKU, who owns it, and what `--check` compares. | When the drift gate is red. |

## Reading order for an agent new to this framework

1. `AGENTS.framework.md` §1 (the 17 rules) and §3 (the two View tests) — these are rejection
   criteria at review, not advice.
2. `architecture-map.md` §1 (assembly graph) and §2 (scope tree) — everything else derives from
   these two.
3. `architecture-map.md` §4 (three-tier init law) — the first question you will hit on day one.
4. The `recipes/` file for the task in front of you.

Do **not** read this pack end to end. It is a reference, indexed by task; the recipes and the API
index exist so that "grep the codebase to figure out the pattern" is never the cheapest path.

## Design constraints this pack is written under

- **Lookup tables, not prose.** A human onboarding doc optimizes for a linear read; this one
  optimizes for a targeted lookup. The narrative version for humans is
  `docs/PrototypeFramework-Architecture-Overview.md` in the framework repo.
- **Always-on budget ≤ ~2k tokens.** Only the synced `AGENTS.md` region and the skill frontmatter
  are permanently in context. Everything else loads on demand.
- **Every claim carries its enforcement.** A rule with no gate is a preference; this pack states
  the gate (a test name, a grep, a CLI exit code) next to the rule so an agent can verify rather
  than trust.
- **The generated half cannot drift.** `framework-api.index.json` is emitted from the package
  sources by the same tool that syncs, and `--check` fails the build when it is stale.

## Precedence when documents disagree

`AGENTS.framework.md` (the rules) > `architecture-map.md` (the shape) > `recipes/` (the
procedures) > any prose doc in the framework repo. Within the framework repo itself the older
precedence still holds for design questions: `ARCHITECTURE-SPINE.md` (invariants AD-1..AD-18) >
`SOLUTION-DESIGN.md` (exact API shapes) > PRD/epics > the original brief.

If this pack and the code disagree, **the code wins and the pack has a bug** — file it as
`Owner: framework/agent-docs` in `deferred-work.md`.
